items.description: ANS-176 — Gitblit near-idle when idle: "Find what it spends the CPU on (Lucene indexing, a ticket or federation poll, a GC loop, the MCP server's queries) and bring it down to near-idle." Settled bar: after the run's push has rolled the pod, gitblit-app averages at most 50m CPU over an hour, read from Prometheus (`http://prometheus.home`, `rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{namespace="git-sync-prd",container="gitblit-app"}[...])`); the hour is one in which a single gitblit pod (the one the push rolled) runs throughout — no second roll inside it — and which does not overlap the 02:00–03:00 Europe/Amsterdam git-sync and the re-index after it; before the fix it ran ≈ 500–600m, and ≈ 200m even in a pre-fix pod's first hours.

The running gitblit-app JVM has explicit GC disabled (`-XX:+DisableExplicitGC`) and still runs with a 1024M heap maximum — shown by the live pod and the JVM's own command line/startup, not only by the rendered chart. Today the container sets no `JAVA_OPTS` (GitSyncDeploy `chart/templates/gitblit-deployment.yaml:72-73`, commented out).

gitblit-app has no CPU request in prd; its `memory: 4096Mi` request is unchanged, and no other container's resources changed (today `config/prd/values.yaml:35-38` requests `cpu: 600m`, `memory: 4096Mi`).

The run pushed the change to GitSyncDeploy `main`; Argo CD Application `argocd-prd/git-sync-prd` is Synced and Healthy on that commit, and the new gitblit pod is Ready with all three containers running and no restarts across the observation hour.
